title: Sanchez’s snap election, and what his (likely) defeat means for Spain’s Nato spending
lede: Prime minister Pedro Sánchez’s rejection of Nato’s five-percent target was less hostile to rearmament than it looks. Military spending rose by 50 percent in 2025, and not even the election campaign slowed this pace down, as earlier this month the Spanish government authorised a further €12.2bn for air defence, counter-drone systems, submarines and ships.
